University of Melbourne.name: Old Quad and the Eight-Hour Day
University of Melbourne.description: The Old Quad was the university's first building, and in 1856 the stonemasons building it downed tools and joined the marches that won the eight-hour working day. Visitors can walk through the Old Quad, the campus's historic heart.

University of Melbourne.name: Spot the Old Arts clock oddity
University of Melbourne.description: Students and visitors are invited to study the Roman numerals on the Old Arts Building clock tower and spot what is odd about them.

University of Melbourne.name: The last piece of the original fence
University of Melbourne.description: A single segment of the wrought-iron fence that once encircled the whole campus survives outside the Medical Building. The grounds were opened to the public in exchange for free gas lighting from the City of Melbourne; visitors can find the remaining fence section.

University of Sydney.name: The Quadrangle jacaranda
University of Sydney.description: Campus folklore says any student who has not started studying before the Quadrangle's jacaranda flowers will fail their exams. Visitors can see the tree (a clone of the 1928 original) bloom purple in late spring, a favourite photo backdrop.

University of Sydney.name: War Memorial Carillon recitals
University of Sydney.description: The clock tower holds the War Memorial Carillon, dedicated in 1928 and one of only three carillons in Australia. Visitors can hear live recitals at lunchtime (outside exam periods and public holidays).

University of Sydney.name: Spot the kangaroo gargoyle
University of Sydney.description: Among the Quadrangle's many gargoyles are Australian animals, including a kangaroo on the clock tower and kookaburras above the northern foyer entrance. Visitors can look for them around the sandstone buildings.

University of Sydney.name: Graffiti Tunnel
University of Sydney.description: The Graffiti Tunnel began as a student protest against the Vietnam War and is now a constantly changing living artwork. Visitors can walk through and see the latest layers of student art.

University of Texas at Austin.name: Tower lighting
University of Texas at Austin.description: Since 1937 the UT Tower has been lit to mark Longhorn achievements: an orange top for football wins, fully orange for big milestones, and orange with a No. 1 for national championships. Visitors can check the Tower at night to see what is being celebrated.

University of Texas at Austin.name: Kniker Carillon
University of Texas at Austin.description: The 56-bell Kniker Carillon at the top of the Tower, the largest in Texas, is played by the student Guild of Carillonneurs, and every set closes with "The Eyes of Texas." Visitors on the Main Mall can listen when the bells are played.

University of Texas at Austin.name: Turtle Pond
University of Texas at Austin.description: Built in 1939 as a biology research pond, Turtle Pond is home to at least 100 turtles, mostly red-eared sliders, and is a favourite campus stop. Visitors can drop by to watch the turtles, which are most active in warm weather.

University of Texas at Austin.name: Tower photo from Littlefield Fountain
University of Texas at Austin.description: The view of the Tower with Littlefield Fountain in the foreground, from 21st Street and University Avenue, is one of the most photographed scenes on campus. Visitors can take the classic shot from the South Mall.

University College London.name: Jeremy Bentham's auto-icon
University College London.description: The preserved skeleton of philosopher Jeremy Bentham, UCL's 'spiritual founder', sits dressed in his own clothes (with a wax head) in a glass case at the entrance of the Student Centre; in 2013 it was even brought to a UCL council meeting. Visitors can see it on public display.

University College London.name: Photo at the Portico
University College London.description: The Portico of the Wilkins Building in the Main Quad is UCL's most photographed and most iconic spot. Visitors can take the classic photo of its columns and dome from the Quad.

University College London.name: Flaxman Gallery under the dome
University College London.description: Beneath the Octagon dome, the Flaxman Gallery holds the largest single collection of works by sculptor John Flaxman, including the full-scale St Michael Overcoming Satan, and appeared in Christopher Nolan's film Inception. Visitors can view the sculptures.

King's College London.name: Reggie the Lion
King's College London.description: Reggie the Lion is the King's mascot and was once paraded at sports matches; after years of being 'lionnapped' by rival students, the original is now displayed in a glass case at the Strand campus. Visitors can see Reggie on display.

King's College London.name: Choral Evensong in the College Chapel
King's College London.description: Choral Evensong is sung in the Grade I listed College Chapel, redesigned by Sir George Gilbert Scott in 1864, on Tuesdays at 5:30pm during term. Visitors can attend the service.

King's College London.name: Bush House friendship inscription
King's College London.description: Bush House, the former BBC World Service home now part of the Strand campus, bears the inscription 'To the friendship of English speaking peoples' above two statues unveiled in 1925. Visitors can view it from Kingsway and take a photo.

University of Paris (Sorbonne).name: Touch Montaigne's Shoe
University of Paris (Sorbonne).description: Across the rue des Écoles from the Sorbonne, students touch the foot of Paul Landowski's seated Montaigne statue for luck before exams. Visitors can stop by the statue and see the shoe polished bright by generations of hands.

University of Paris (Sorbonne).name: Richelieu's Cardinal Hat
University of Paris (Sorbonne).description: In the Sorbonne Chapel, a cardinal's hat hangs above Cardinal Richelieu's marble tomb, as tradition dictates. Visitors can see it when the chapel opens for guided tours and Heritage Days.

University of Paris (Sorbonne).name: Heritage Days at the Sorbonne
University of Paris (Sorbonne).description: Each September during the European Heritage Days, the Sorbonne opens its reception halls and Grand Amphitheatre to the public for free. Visitors can walk up onto the amphitheatre's stage and tour rooms that are normally closed.

University of Padua.name: Galileo's Lectern
University of Padua.description: The wooden lectern Galileo is said to have lectured from, built for him by his own students according to tradition, stands at the entrance of the Sala dei Quaranta in Palazzo Bo. Visitors can see it on a guided tour of the palace.

University of Padua.name: Don't Jump the Chain
University of Padua.description: Local superstition holds that students should never jump over the chain in front of Palazzo Bo, or their studies will suffer. Visitors can see the chain and step around it.

University of Padua.name: Caffè Pedrocchi
University of Padua.description: The historic café beside Palazzo Bo has been a meeting place for students and professors since 1831, and students may sit in its green room without buying anything. Visitors can stop for its mint coffee and look for the bullet hole left from the 1848 student uprising in the white room.

KU Leuven.name: Fonske
KU Leuven.description: Fons Sapientiae ('Fountain of Wisdom') is a statue of a student pouring wisdom into his head while reading, given to the city by the university for its 550th anniversary in 1975. Student societies dress it up for special occasions, and visitors can stop for a photo on Rector De Somerplein.

KU Leuven.name: University Library Carillon
KU Leuven.description: The University Library tower holds one of Europe's largest carillons, a memorial gift from American engineers, and its main bell rings every hour. On tower visits the carillonneur takes visitors up to hear a live concert from the front row.

KU Leuven.name: Totem on Ladeuzeplein
KU Leuven.description: For its 575th anniversary in 2004, the university gave the city Jan Fabre's Totem, a giant jewel beetle stuck on a 23 m steel needle in front of the University Library. Visitors can take a photo of it on Ladeuzeplein.

Aalto University.name: Museum of Student Life
Aalto University.description: In a basement in the Otaniemi student village, the student union's museum (formerly the Polyteekkarimuseo) shows teekkari and other Aalto student traditions, from caps and overalls to famous pranks. Volunteer guides open it to visitors on Sunday afternoons during term.

Aalto University.name: Otaniemi Chapel Forest View
Aalto University.description: Heikki and Kaija Siren's 1956 campus chapel has a glass wall behind the altar that looks onto the forest and a cross set into the bedrock outside. The university lists the view as one of the most popular sights in Otaniemi.

Uppsala University.name: Walpurgis Cap Raising
Uppsala University.description: At 3 pm on 30 April, students on the slope below the Carolina Rediviva library put on their white student caps together as the rector waves his cap from the library balcony. Anyone can join the crowd on the hill to watch.

Uppsala University.name: Spring Song at Gunillaklockan
Uppsala University.description: On the evening of 30 April, students gather at the Gunilla bell beside Uppsala Castle for the spring song and the spring speech. Visitors can stand with the crowd and listen.

Uppsala University.name: Gustavianum Anatomical Theatre
Uppsala University.description: Under the copper cupola of the Gustavianum, the university museum preserves the anatomical theatre Olof Rudbeck the Elder built in the 1660s. Visitors can step inside it as part of a museum visit.

Florida Southern College.name: Annie Pfeiffer Chapel
Florida Southern College.description: The college calls Frank Lloyd Wright's chapel the soaring heart of the campus; it is crowned by a bell tower of concrete and colored glass. Visitors can see it on a guided Wright tour that starts at the Sharp Family Tourism and Education Center.

Florida Southern College.name: Water Dome Fountains
Florida Southern College.description: Wright's largest water feature was finally built to his full design in 2007, and its fountains run at set times during the day. Visitors can view it at any time from the surrounding esplanades.

Boston College.name: Golden Eagle Statue
Boston College.description: A gilded eagle on a 30-foot column stands in front of Gasson Hall, a replica of the statue the college received in 1954. Visitors take a photo of the eagle with Gasson Tower behind it.

Boston College.name: Doug Flutie Statue
Boston College.description: A statue outside Alumni Stadium recreates the Hail Mary pass that made quarterback Doug Flutie famous. Fans stop for a photo with it on the way to the stadium.

Clemson University.name: Howard's Rock
Clemson University.description: This piece of quartzite sits on a pedestal atop The Hill in Memorial Stadium, and players rub it before running down onto the field at home games. Visitors can see it at the east end of the stadium.

Clemson University.name: Lover's Lane in President's Park
Clemson University.description: Campus legend says couples who walk hand in hand through President's Park will marry. Visitors stroll the park at the edge of campus.

Clemson University.name: Bowman Field
Clemson University.description: Bowman Field, the lawn in front of Tillman Hall, was the parade ground for Clemson's cadets. Visitors take in the view of the Tillman Hall clock tower from the field.

Duke University.name: Duke Chapel Carillon
Duke University.description: The 50-bell carillon in the Duke Chapel tower is played every weekday at 5 p.m., and the alma mater is played on Fridays. Visitors gather near the chapel to listen.

Duke University.name: Krzyzewskiville
Duke University.description: Before the biggest men's basketball games, students camp in a tent city called Krzyzewskiville on the lawn beside Cameron Indoor Stadium. Visitors in winter can walk past the tents.

Florida State University.name: Unconquered Statue
Florida State University.description: This bronze statue outside Doak Campbell Stadium shows a Seminole rider on a rearing horse. Its spear is lit at sunset before home football games, and fans gather to watch.

Florida State University.name: Legacy Walk
Florida State University.description: Medallions and garnet banners mark a walking tour of campus history that starts at Landis Green. Visitors follow it past historic buildings, statues and monuments.

Georgia Institute of Technology.name: Tech Tower
Georgia Institute of Technology.description: The lighted TECH letters on all four sides of Tech Tower are the best-known symbol of the institute. Visitors take a photo from the lawn below; taking the letters is banned.

Georgia Institute of Technology.name: Kessler Campanile
Georgia Institute of Technology.description: This 80-foot stainless steel campanile in front of the student center was built for the 1996 Olympics, and its peaks echo Tech Tower. Visitors meet and take photos at its base.

University of Louisville.name: The Thinker
University of Louisville.description: A large bronze cast of Rodin's The Thinker has sat in front of Grawemeyer Hall since 1949. Having your picture taken with it is a classic stop on a campus visit.

University of Miami.name: U Statue at the Rock
University of Miami.description: The U statue on the Rock Plaza, beside the Shalala Student Center, is the classic campus photo spot. Visitors take a picture in front of it.

University of Miami.name: Homecoming Boat Burning
University of Miami.description: Since 1956 a boat has been burned on Lake Osceola at Homecoming. Legend says that if the mast falls before the boat sinks, the Hurricanes will win the next day's game.

University of Miami.name: Bronze Ibis
University of Miami.description: A bronze statue of Sebastian the Ibis, the university mascot, stands in front of the Newman Alumni Center. Visitors stop for a photo with it.

North Carolina State University.name: Belltower Lit Red
North Carolina State University.description: When NC State wins a major sporting event, the Memorial Belltower is lit red. Fans gather at its base to chant and make the Wolfpack hand sign.

North Carolina State University.name: Free Expression Tunnel
North Carolina State University.description: Anyone is allowed to paint the walls, ceiling and floor of this pedestrian tunnel under the railroad between North and Central Campus. Visitors walk through to see the latest messages.

University of North Carolina at Chapel H.name: Sip from the Old Well
University of North Carolina at Chapel H.description: Campus tradition says a drink from the fountain at the Old Well on the first day of classes brings good luck. Visitors can take a sip from the fountain any day.

University of North Carolina at Chapel H.name: Davie Poplar
University of North Carolina at Chapel H.description: Legend says the university will thrive as long as this centuries-old tulip poplar in McCorkle Place stands. Visitors stop to see the tree.

University of North Carolina at Chapel H.name: Bell Tower in Carolina Blue
University of North Carolina at Chapel H.description: The Morehead-Patterson Bell Tower is lit Carolina blue after Tar Heel football wins. Visitors can see the 172-foot tower on the south side of campus.

University of Pittsburgh.name: Victory Lights
University of Pittsburgh.description: The top of the Cathedral of Learning glows gold after Pitt football wins and other championships, with a blue beam added in 2018. Visitors can see it across Oakland.

University of Pittsburgh.name: Panther Statue
University of Pittsburgh.description: The panther statue at the William Pitt Union has a worn nose from years of students rubbing it for good luck. Visitors rub it too.

University of Pittsburgh.name: Heinz Chapel Steps
University of Pittsburgh.description: The steps in front of Heinz Memorial Chapel are said to be a good luck charm for young couples. Visitors take a photo on them.

Southern Methodist University.name: SMU Seal in Dallas Hall
Southern Methodist University.description: The SMU seal is set into the rotunda floor of Dallas Hall. First-year students walk around it at the Rotunda Passage and across it at graduation; visitors can see it in the rotunda.

Southern Methodist University.name: Celebration of Lights
Southern Methodist University.description: At the holiday Celebration of Lights, Dallas Hall is covered in thousands of lights. Guests gather on the lawn for cocoa and cookies, and the evening ends with Silent Night.

Syracuse University.name: Kissing Bench
Syracuse University.description: This granite bench between Tolley Hall and the Hall of Languages was a gift from the class of 1912. Legend says a couple who kisses on it will marry, and anyone who sits there alone will stay single.

Syracuse University.name: Crouse Chimes
Syracuse University.description: The chimes in the tower of Crouse College have rung since 1889 and are played twice a day and on special occasions. Visitors listen from the Quad below.

Virginia Tech.name: Corps of Cadets Retreat
Virginia Tech.description: The Corps of Cadets holds its nightly retreat ceremony in front of Lane Hall, the old Barracks No. 1. Visitors can watch from the Upper Quad.

Wake Forest University.name: Wait Chapel Carillon
Wake Forest University.description: Wait Chapel's tower holds a 12-ton carillon of 48 bronze bells, and the chapel has hosted presidential debates. Visitors see it at the head of the Quad.

Wake Forest University.name: Stone Arch
Wake Forest University.description: This arch on the Quad is a replica of the one on the Old Campus in Wake Forest, North Carolina, and each graduating class walks through it at Commencement. Visitors can walk through it too.

Wake Forest University.name: The Magnolias
Wake Forest University.description: The magnolias on Manchester Plaza grew from seeds collected on the Old Campus in 1947. Visitors walk among them on the lower quad.

University of Arizona.name: Bear Down Gym
University of Arizona.description: "Bear Down," the school's rallying cry, comes from a 1926 message from dying student body president John "Button" Salmon to his team, and Bear Down Gym, the old men's gymnasium, carries the name. Stop by the gym where the slogan lives on.

Arizona State University.name: Palm Walk
Arizona State University.description: Palm Walk links the north and south ends of the Tempe campus and is its most popular corridor, lined with palms taller than 70 feet. Walk its length and take a photo under the palms.

Arizona State University.name: Bronze Pitchfork
Arizona State University.description: A 6-foot-3 bronze pitchfork stands at the southeast entrance of the football stadium. Pose beside it and make the "Fork 'em" hand sign.

Brigham Young University.name: Brigham Young Statue
Brigham Young University.description: A statue of Brigham Young by his grandson, sculptor Mahonri Young, stands in front of the Abraham O. Smoot Administration Building. Visit the statue of the man the school is named for.

Brigham Young University.name: Stadium Cougar Statue
Brigham Young University.description: A bronze cougar, cast in Italy and given by the classes of 1965 and 1969, guards LaVell Edwards Stadium on the northeast end of campus. Take a photo with it.

Brigham Young University.name: Hourly Carillon Tune
Brigham Young University.description: At the top of every hour the Centennial Carillon tolls the first lines of a tune based on the hymn "Come, Come, Ye Saints." Stand near the tower on the hour to hear it.

University of Houston.name: Rub the Paw
University of Houston.description: Before big games, fans rub the paws of the two bronze cougar statues in Cullen Family Plaza in front of the E. Cullen Building for luck. Some students rub them before final exams too.

University of Houston.name: Gate 2 Cougar
University of Houston.description: On game days, fans also rub the paw of the cougar statue at Gate 2 of the football stadium. Give it a rub for luck.

Iowa State University.name: Don't Step on the Zodiac
Iowa State University.description: A bronze zodiac is set in the floor of Gold Star Hall in the Memorial Union. Legend says stepping on it means failing your next exam, so walk around it like generations of students.

Iowa State University.name: Campaniling
Iowa State University.description: Tradition says you become a true Iowa Stater when you are kissed under the Campanile at midnight, and hundreds gather for "Mass Campaniling" at Homecoming. Visit the Campanile and listen for its bells.

Iowa State University.name: Lake LaVerne
Iowa State University.description: Swans first came to Lake LaVerne in 1935 and were named Lancelot and Elaine. Legend says couples who walk silently around the lake three times are meant to be together.

University of Kansas.name: Memorial Campanile
University of Kansas.description: Graduates walk through the World War II Memorial Campanile on their way down the Hill at commencement. Legend says walking through it before then means you won't graduate, so admire it from outside.

University of Kansas.name: Strong Hall Jayhawk
University of Kansas.description: The bronze Jayhawk outside Strong Hall was a gift from the class of 1956. Stop for a photo with it.

Kansas State University.name: Call Hall Ice Cream
Kansas State University.description: K-State's own dairy plant makes more than 40 ice cream flavors, including "Purple Pride," sold at Call Hall. Stop in for a scoop.

Oklahoma State University.name: Edmon Low Library Lawn Photo
Oklahoma State University.description: New students pose for a first-day photo on the lawn in front of Edmon Low Library. Take your own photo in front of the library.

Oklahoma State University.name: Old Central Bell
Oklahoma State University.description: When news of a 1917 football win reached Stillwater, Old Central's bell rang for hours, starting the Bedlam bell tradition. Visit the first permanent building on campus.

Oklahoma State University.name: Theta Pond
Oklahoma State University.description: Theta Pond began as a reservoir in 1895 and is now one of the most scenic spots on campus. Take a walk around it.

Texas Tech University.name: Victory Bells
Texas Tech University.description: The Victory Bells in the east tower of the Administration Building ring after every Texas Tech athletic win and at graduations. Listen for them after a win.

Texas Tech University.name: Carol of Lights
Texas Tech University.description: Since 1959, Texas Tech has covered the Administration Building and nearby buildings in holiday lights each December. Come see the lights at the start of the season.

Texas Tech University.name: Masked Rider Statue
Texas Tech University.description: A larger-than-life sculpture by Grant Speed honoring the Masked Rider mascot stands outside the Frazier Alumni Pavilion. Take a photo with it.

West Virginia University.name: Woodburn Hall Holiday Lighting
West Virginia University.description: WVU lights up Woodburn Hall for the holidays, a campus tradition revived in 2025. Visit in December to see it lit.

West Virginia University.name: Mountaineer Statue
West Virginia University.description: Sculptor Donald De Lue's 1971 bronze statue of the Mountaineer stands at the Mountainlair student union. Find it and take a photo.

Baylor University.name: Judge Baylor Statue
Baylor University.description: A bronze statue of Judge R.E.B. Baylor on Founders Mall faces Waco Hall and is a favorite campus photo spot. Take a photo with the school's namesake.

Baylor University.name: McLane Carillon
Baylor University.description: The 48-bell McLane Carillon at Pat Neff Hall, a gift from the McLane family in 1988, fills the campus with music. Listen for it near Pat Neff Hall.

University of Cincinnati.name: Bearcat Statue
University of Cincinnati.description: The 15-foot bronze Bearcat by Jon Hair, a gift of the Sigma Sigma honorary in 2010, is a favorite photo backdrop for campus tours and graduates. It stands on Commons Way outside Marian Spencer Hall.

University of Colorado Boulder.name: Norlin Library Inscriptions
University of Colorado Boulder.description: Two inscriptions by President George Norlin are carved on the library's west face over Norlin Quadrangle: "Who knows only his own generation remains always a child" and, over the door, "Enter here the timeless fellowship of the human spirit." Read them from the quad.

University of Colorado Boulder.name: CU Heritage Center in Old Main
University of Colorado Boulder.description: Old Main, the first building on campus, houses the CU Heritage Center, whose galleries tell the university's history. Visit to see the stories of CU's past.

Texas Christian University.name: Lucky Horned Frog Statue
Texas Christian University.description: Students rub the nose of the welded Horned Frog statue by Seppo Aarnos, installed in 1984 between Sadler and Reed halls, for luck before tests. Give it a rub.

Texas Christian University.name: Frog Fountain
Texas Christian University.description: Seniors and their families take cap-and-gown photos at Frog Fountain, and fireworks light the sky over it when the Frogs score at home games. Take a photo at the fountain.

Texas Christian University.name: Carols by Candlelight
Texas Christian University.description: For more than 40 years, Carols by Candlelight has been held each December in Robert Carr Chapel. Visit the chapel during the holiday season.

University of Central Florida.name: Don't Step on the Seal
University of Central Florida.description: Legend says you won't graduate if you walk across the Pegasus seal in the Student Union, though graduates may cross it once they have their diplomas. Find the seal and walk around it.

University of Utah.name: Block U
University of Utah.description: The Block U on the hillside above campus, first built in 1907, lights up for home athletic events, flashing red after home wins in football, basketball and gymnastics. Look up at the hill after a win.

University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign.name: Alma Mater Statue
University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign.description: Lorado Taft's 1929 bronze of a robed woman with outstretched arms stands by Altgeld Hall to welcome students. Stop for a photo with her, a classic Illinois picture.

University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign.name: Altgeld Chimes
University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign.description: The chime of 15 bells in Altgeld Hall's tower has rung since 1920, marking the hours and playing short concerts. Listen near the tower for "Hail to the Orange," played at every concert.

University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign.name: Morrow Plots
University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign.description: Planted in 1876, these small fields are the oldest agricultural experiment fields in the United States and a National Historic Landmark. Walk past them beside the Undergraduate Library.

Indiana University Bloomington.name: Rose Well House
Indiana University Bloomington.description: Campus legend says a kiss under the Rose Well House at midnight brings lasting romance. The little pavilion near Dunn Woods is also a favorite spot for proposals.

Indiana University Bloomington.name: Sample Gates
Indiana University Bloomington.description: The limestone Sample Gates mark the entrance to the Old Crescent from Kirkwood Avenue. Walk through them and take a photo, as many new graduates do.

Indiana University Bloomington.name: Herman B Wells Statue
Indiana University Bloomington.description: A bronze of the beloved former president sits on a bench with his hand held out. Shake it: the story goes that a student whose family shakes his hand will graduate on time.

Indiana University Bloomington.name: Showalter Fountain
Indiana University Bloomington.description: The fountain in the Fine Arts Plaza shows the birth of Venus surrounded by bronze fish. Count the fish and look for the one that replaced a fish taken after the 1987 basketball title.

University of Iowa.name: Old Capitol Photo
University of Iowa.description: Graduates like to pose in front of the Old Capitol, by its columns and the doorway with "Iowa" above it. Take your own photo on the steps at the heart of the Pentacrest.

University of Iowa.name: Kinnick Wave
University of Iowa.description: At home football games, after the first quarter the whole crowd turns and waves to the patients watching from the children's hospital above the east stands. If you go to a game, join in.

University of Maryland, College Park.name: Rub Testudo's Nose
University of Maryland, College Park.description: Students rub the nose of the bronze terrapin Testudo outside McKeldin Library for luck, and leave small offerings during finals. Give his nose a rub as you pass.

Michigan State University.name: The Rock
Michigan State University.description: Given by the Class of 1873, the Rock beside the Red Cedar River is painted over again and again with new messages. Stop to see what it says today.

Michigan State University.name: The Spartan Statue
Michigan State University.description: The nearly 10-foot bronze Spartan is a favorite photo backdrop, especially at graduation. Take a selfie with it.

Michigan State University.name: Beaumont Tower Open Tower
Michigan State University.description: Beaumont Tower opens to visitors on the first Wednesday of each month and at graduation. Go up to see the carillon and the view over campus.

Michigan State University.name: MSU Dairy Store
Michigan State University.description: The MSU Dairy Store was voted Grand Champion in the American Dairy Science Association's 2025 Ice Cream Competition. Stop at its Anthony Hall shop and try a flavor.

Michigan State University.name: W. J. Beal Botanical Garden
Michigan State University.description: Professor William J. Beal began this garden in 1873, and it is claimed to be the oldest continuously maintained university botanical garden in the US. Stroll it for free any day during daylight hours.

Michigan State University.name: MSU Horticulture Gardens
Michigan State University.description: The gardens on Bogue Street hold more than 700 rose cultivars and the Michigan 4-H Children's Garden. Wander them for free any day.

Michigan State University.name: Red Cedar River Trail
Michigan State University.description: A trail runs across campus along the south bank of the Red Cedar River, and the Lansing River Trail starts here. Bike or walk it, or kayak the river.

Michigan State University.name: The Izzone
Michigan State University.description: Named for coach Tom Izzo, the Izzone is the student section of about 5,000 at men's basketball games in the Breslin Center. Catch a game to hear it roar.

Michigan State University.name: Magic Johnson Statue
Michigan State University.description: A 12-foot bronze of Earvin "Magic" Johnson, who led MSU to the 1979 national title, has stood outside the Breslin Center since 2003. Snap a photo with it.

Michigan State University.name: Spartan Marching Band March
Michigan State University.description: On football Saturdays the band warms up on Adams Field, then marches past the Spartan Statue and up Red Cedar Road to the stadium about an hour before kickoff. Line the route to cheer it on.

University of Minnesota Twin Cities.name: Goldy Gopher Statue
University of Minnesota Twin Cities.description: A bronze Goldy Gopher stands beside a granite M outside Coffman Memorial Union, a gathering spot and a symbol of school spirit. Stop by for a photo.

University of Nebraska–Lincoln.name: Archie the Mammoth
University of Nebraska–Lincoln.description: Students rub the foot of Archie, the bronze mammoth outside Morrill Hall, for luck before tests and projects. Give his foot a rub or a high-five.

Northwestern University.name: The Rock
Northwestern University.description: Students have painted the Rock since the 1940s, often guarding it for a day before painting it overnight. Stop by to see the latest message.

Northwestern University.name: Weber Arch
Northwestern University.description: New students march in through Weber Arch at the start of their time at Northwestern, and seniors march out through it near the end. Walk through the arch from Sheridan Road onto campus.

Northwestern University.name: Shakespeare Garden
Northwestern University.description: This quiet garden on the north side of campus is one of the stops on the admissions campus tour map. Visit it on a walk through campus.

Ohio State University.name: The Long Walk
Ohio State University.description: The Long Walk crosses the Oval toward University Hall; first-year students were once forbidden to use it. Walk its length across the heart of campus.

Ohio State University.name: Buckeye Grove
Ohio State University.description: A buckeye tree is planted beside Ohio Stadium for each of Ohio State's first-team All-Americans, each with a plaque. Look for the names of famous players among the trees.

Ohio State University.name: Victory Bell
Ohio State University.description: The Victory Bell in Ohio Stadium's southeast tower is rung after every Ohio State win. Listen for it after a home game.

Pennsylvania State University.name: Nittany Lion Shrine
Pennsylvania State University.description: Heinz Warneke's limestone lion, dedicated in 1942, is the most photographed spot on campus. Many students take a photo here on their first day and again before graduation.

Pennsylvania State University.name: Berkey Creamery
Pennsylvania State University.description: The university's creamery, whose ice cream short course dates back to 1892, sells its own ice cream in the Food Science Building. Stop in for a cone.

Purdue University.name: Bell Tower Kiss
Purdue University.description: Legend says a couple who kiss under the Bell Tower and then walk past the nearby Stone Lion Fountain will one day marry. Visit the tower at the center of campus.

Purdue University.name: Hello Walk
Purdue University.description: The Hello Walk began as the path to University Hall and now covers the walks across Memorial Mall. Smile and say hello to everyone you pass.

Rutgers University–New Brunswick.name: Willie the Silent
Rutgers University–New Brunswick.description: The 1928 bronze of William the Silent, Prince of Orange, known to students as Willie the Silent, is one of the best-loved statues on campus. Find him on Voorhees Mall.

Rutgers University–New Brunswick.name: Old Queens Bell
Rutgers University–New Brunswick.description: The bell in the cupola of Old Queens rings for convocation, commencement and other great occasions, and inspired the song "The Bells Must Ring." Look up at the cupola from the Queens Campus.

University of Wisconsin–Madison.name: Abe Lincoln on Bascom Hill
University of Wisconsin–Madison.description: The seated Abraham Lincoln statue in front of Bascom Hall is a highlight of commencement weekend photos. Take your picture beside him at the top of the hill.

University of Wisconsin–Madison.name: Terrace Sunburst Chairs
University of Wisconsin–Madison.description: The sunburst chairs on the Memorial Union Terrace are one of the university's best-known symbols. Sit in one by Lake Mendota.

University of Wisconsin–Madison.name: Babcock Hall Ice Cream
University of Wisconsin–Madison.description: Ice cream made by the university's dairy at Babcock Hall is a student staple and a visitor favorite. Try a scoop.

University of Oregon.name: Yell-O Duck Statue
University of Oregon.description: A 1,000-pound bronze of the Duck throwing the "O" stands between Matthew Knight Arena and the Ford Alumni Center. Throw the O beside it for a photo.

University of Oregon.name: Bill Bowerman Statue
University of Oregon.description: A 2000 bronze of coach and Nike co-founder Bill Bowerman stands at the corner of Hayward Field. Visit it on a walk around the track stadium.

University of Southern California.name: Tommy Trojan
University of Southern California.description: The bronze Trojan warrior in Hahn Plaza is the campus's favorite meeting place. Before the UCLA game it is wrapped in duct tape and guarded around the clock by the Trojan Knights.

University of Southern California.name: Hecuba Statue
University of Southern California.description: The statue of Hecuba, queen of Troy, was unveiled in 2017 in the central plaza of USC Village as a counterpart to Tommy Trojan. Visit her in the plaza.

University of Alabama.name: Walk of Fame at Denny Chimes
University of Alabama.description: Since 1948, Alabama's football captains have pressed their handprints and footprints into the concrete around the base of Denny Chimes. Walk around the tower to find the names, and listen for the Westminster chimes every 15 minutes.

University of Alabama.name: Walk of Champions
University of Alabama.description: Outside Bryant–Denny Stadium, granite slabs list the Crimson Tide's national championships beside statues of championship coaches. On game days fans line the walk to cheer the team as it arrives.

University of Arkansas.name: Senior Walk
University of Arkansas.description: The campus sidewalks carry the names of the university's graduates, class by class, going back to 1876. Start near Old Main and look down to read the names.

University of Arkansas.name: Spoofer's Stone
University of Arkansas.description: This limestone rock near Old Main dates from a time when men and women students were not allowed to mingle, and they left love notes in its cracks. It is now a popular spot for marriage proposals.

Auburn University.name: Toomer's Corner
Auburn University.description: Where College Street meets Magnolia Avenue, fans celebrate Auburn wins by rolling the oaks with toilet paper, a celebration the university endorses. Visit the corner and the replanted Toomer's Oaks, or come after a win to watch.

Auburn University.name: Tiger Walk
Auburn University.description: Before home football games, fans line Donahue Drive to cheer the team as it walks into Jordan-Hare Stadium. Auburn calls it one of the most copied traditions in college football.

University of Florida.name: Century Tower carillon
University of Florida.description: The 61-bell carillon in Century Tower, completed in its present form in 2003, rings out over the center of campus. Stand on the lawn below to listen.

University of Georgia.name: The Arch
University of Georgia.description: The Arch is the gateway between North Campus and downtown Athens. By legend, students do not walk under it until they graduate, so many visitors walk around it and take a photo instead.

University of Georgia.name: Chapel Bell
University of Georgia.description: The bell beside the Chapel has been rung to celebrate football wins since 1894. The university encourages ringing it for athletic victories and other special occasions.

Louisiana State University.name: Mike the Tiger's habitat
Louisiana State University.description: LSU has kept a live tiger on campus since 1936. Visit Mike in his habitat between Tiger Stadium and the Pete Maravich Assembly Center, which is open to visitors year-round.

Louisiana State University.name: Victory Hill march
Louisiana State University.description: Before home games, fans line Victory Hill to watch the team, coaches and the Golden Band march from the Greek Theatre toward Tiger Stadium.

University of Mississippi.name: Walk of Champions
University of Mississippi.description: Before every Saturday home game, the team walks through the Grove from the Walk of Champions arch, a 1998 gift from the unbeaten 1962 team. Fans line the path to cheer them on.

University of Mississippi.name: Civil Rights Monument
University of Mississippi.description: Between the Lyceum and the library, a life-size statue of James Meredith, the first Black student admitted to the university, stands with a limestone portal carved with the words Courage, Knowledge, Perseverance and Opportunity.

University of Mississippi.name: The Grove
University of Mississippi.description: This 10-acre park shaded by oaks sits at the center of campus. Stroll through it, and on game days hear the Pride of the South play its pregame show at the Grove stage.

University of Missouri.name: Walk through the Columns
University of Missouri.description: Each August, new students sprint through the Columns toward Jesse Hall, and graduating seniors walk back the other way in May. Visitors can walk the same route across Francis Quadrangle.

University of Missouri.name: David R. Francis's nose
University of Missouri.description: By legend, rubbing the nose on the bronze relief of David R. Francis near the northeast entrance of Jesse Hall brings an A on the next exam. Francis is credited with keeping the university in Columbia after the 1892 fire.

University of Missouri.name: Thomas Jefferson's tombstone
University of Missouri.description: The original marker from Thomas Jefferson's grave at Monticello stands on the east side of Francis Quadrangle. His heirs gave it to Mizzou in 1883 as the first university founded in the Louisiana Purchase territory.

University of Oklahoma.name: The Seed Sower
University of Oklahoma.description: A 12-foot bronze Seed Sower by Paul Moore stands by the South Oval, based on the figure in the university seal and a parable told by first president David Ross Boyd. It is dressed up when the team learns its bowl destination.

University of Oklahoma.name: Heisman Park
University of Oklahoma.description: On the east side of the football stadium, bronze statues honor Oklahoma's Heisman Trophy winners. It is a popular spot for photos.

University of South Carolina.name: Maxcy Monument
University of South Carolina.description: At the center of the Horseshoe stands the monument to Jonathan Maxcy, the first president, designed by Robert Mills and dedicated in 1827. Read the Latin inscriptions and the English translations nearby.

University of South Carolina.name: Cocky statue
University of South Carolina.description: A statue of the Gamecock mascot stands off Greene Street near the Russell House, and visitors are invited to take a photo with it.

Vanderbilt University.name: Commodore Vanderbilt statue
Vanderbilt University.description: The statue of Cornelius Vanderbilt, whose gift founded the university, stands at the north end of the esplanade facing West End Avenue. The statue is a site for Founder's Day ceremonies around March 17, the anniversary of the founding.

University of Kentucky.name: Bowman the Wildcat
University of Kentucky.description: The bronze Wildcat statue in Wildcat Alumni Plaza was named Bowman by student vote in 2012. Visitors pat his head and rub his nose and paws for good luck.

Mississippi State University.name: Cowbells at Davis Wade Stadium
Mississippi State University.description: Fans ring cowbells at Mississippi State games, the most famous symbol of the school's spirit. Bring a cowbell to a home game, or hear them at the Cowbell Yell pep rally in the stadium.

Mississippi State University.name: The Drill Field
Mississippi State University.description: The main quadrangle is named for its use by the Corps of Cadets. Students relax here between classes, and the Drill pep rally is held on it in the first week of classes.

University of Tennessee.name: The Torchbearer
University of Tennessee.description: The Torchbearer statue in Circle Park carries the Volunteer Creed on its plaque. Read the creed, the source of the university's Torch Night ceremony.

University of Tennessee.name: The Rock
University of Tennessee.description: This large limestone boulder is painted over and over by students with messages, from birthdays to marriage proposals. Stop by to see what it says today.

University of Tennessee.name: Vol Walk
University of Tennessee.description: Before home games, fans line the route as the team walks from the Torchbearer to Neyland Stadium, led by the band. The tradition dates to 1990.

Texas A&M University.name: Pennies on Sully
Texas A&M University.description: Students leave pennies at the base of the statue of Lawrence Sullivan Ross for luck before exams, recalling his reply "a penny for your thoughts." The coins are given to charity each semester.

Texas A&M University.name: Century Tree
Texas A&M University.description: This live oak, one of the first trees planted on campus, is well over 100 years old. By legend, a couple who walk beneath it together will marry.

University of Oxford.name: Great Tom's 101 Strokes
University of Oxford.description: Every night at 9:05pm (9pm old 'Oxford time') the Great Tom bell in Christ Church's Tom Tower rings 101 times, once for each of the college's original 100 scholars plus one added in 1663. Stand on St Aldate's to hear it.

University of Oxford.name: May Morning at Magdalen Tower
University of Oxford.description: At 6am on 1 May the Magdalen College Choir sings the Hymnus Eucharisticus from the top of the Great Tower, a ceremony going back about 500 years. Crowds gather on the High Street and Magdalen Bridge below to listen.

University of Oxford.name: Bridge of Sighs
University of Oxford.description: Hertford Bridge, nicknamed the Bridge of Sighs after the Venice bridge it is said to resemble, links two parts of Hertford College over New College Lane. Stop on the lane to see and photograph this city landmark.

University of Cambridge.name: Nine Lessons and Carols at King's
University of Cambridge.description: On Christmas Eve the King's College Choir sings the Festival of Nine Lessons and Carols in King's College Chapel. Tickets come from a public ballot, with a standby queue for people who applied.

University of Cambridge.name: Corpus Clock
University of Cambridge.description: The Corpus Clock, or Chronophage, is a gold-plated clock with no hands, set at street level on Corpus Christi College's Taylor Library at the corner of Bene't Street and Trumpington Street. Stop to watch its grasshopper-like figure as the clock runs.

University of Cambridge.name: Mathematical Bridge Myth
University of Cambridge.description: A popular fable says Isaac Newton built Queens' College's Mathematical Bridge without nuts or bolts, and that nobody could put it back together after taking it apart. View the bridge from the river or Silver Street and judge the story yourself.

University of Cambridge.name: Newton's Apple Tree
University of Cambridge.description: Outside Trinity College's Great Gate, below the rooms where Newton lived, grows an apple tree planted in 1954 and descended from the Woolsthorpe Manor tree linked to his story of gravity. Visitors stop on Trinity Street to see it.

University of Cambridge.name: Henry VIII's Chair Leg
University of Cambridge.description: The statue of Henry VIII on Trinity's Great Gate is famous because students swapped his sceptre for a chair leg in the 19th century. Look up from Trinity Street to see what he is holding.

University of St Andrews.name: Patrick Hamilton's PH
University of St Andrews.description: The letters PH set in the cobbles outside St Salvator's Quad mark where Patrick Hamilton was burned at the stake in 1528. Tradition says any student who steps on them will fail their degree, so visitors step around them too.

University of St Andrews.name: Pier Walk
University of St Andrews.description: After chapel each week, students in red gowns walk the length of the historic harbour pier, with the busiest walk at the end of Freshers' Week. Visitors can watch the procession or walk the pier themselves.

University of Glasgow.name: Rub the Unicorn's Horn
University of Glasgow.description: The Lion and Unicorn Staircase, carved in 1690, was moved stone by stone from the Old College on the High Street. Patting the unicorn or rubbing its horn is said to bring good luck, especially before exams.

University of Glasgow.name: Keep Off the Quad Grass
University of Glasgow.description: It is thought to be bad luck for students to walk on the grass of the quadrangles before they graduate. Visitors can admire the East and West Quads from the paths, where graduation processions led by a piper take place.

University of Glasgow.name: The Cloisters
University of Glasgow.description: The vaulted Cloisters (the Undercroft) between the East and West Quadrangles have appeared in films and TV series including Outlander and Cloud Atlas. Walk through and take a photo under the fluted columns.

University of Edinburgh.name: Rub David Hume's Toe
University of Edinburgh.description: Former Edinburgh student David Hume's statue on the Royal Mile has a toe polished bright by students, tourists and passers-by rubbing it for luck. Visitors can give it a rub, though Hume himself was a famous critic of superstition.

University of Edinburgh.name: Spot the Gilded Youth on Old College
University of Edinburgh.description: The dome of Old College, added in 1887, is crowned by John Hutchison's gilded statue of Youth. Visitors can look up at it from South Bridge or walk into the quadrangle, which also hosts graduation ceremonies and festival events.

Durham University.name: See the Sanctuary Knocker
Durham University.description: In medieval times, anyone who had committed a great offence could grasp the ring on Durham Cathedral's north door and claim 37 days of sanctuary. Visitors can see the replica ring on the north door; the 12th-century original is in the Cathedral Museum.

Durham University.name: Tour the Castle College
Durham University.description: Durham Castle on Palace Green is home to University College, where about 150 students live and formal dinners are still held in the medieval Great Hall. Visitors can see inside on a guided tour, which runs daily outside term time.

Durham University.name: Find the Dun Cow
Durham University.description: Local legend says monks carrying St Cuthbert's body followed a milkmaid looking for her lost dun cow to the hill where the cathedral now stands. Dun Cow Lane, beside the cathedral, takes its name from a carving of the story on the cathedral, and visitors can look for it.

Trinity College Dublin.name: Don't Walk Under the Campanile
Trinity College Dublin.description: Student superstition says that anyone who walks under the Campanile in Front Square while its bell tolls will fail their exams, so students rarely shelter beneath it, even in rain. Visitors can watch students walk around it rather than through it.

Trinity College Dublin.name: See the Book of Kells and the Long Room
Trinity College Dublin.description: The Old Library has held the Book of Kells since 1661, and its Long Room gets over 900,000 visitors a year. Visitors can buy a ticket to see the manuscript and walk through the Long Room.

Wayne State University.name: Friday Night Planetarium Show
Wayne State University.description: The Wayne State Planetarium in Old Main puts on free public shows most Friday evenings, with a tour of the current night sky and a fulldome film. Arrive early, since seats are first come, first served.

Wayne State University.name: Old Main's Peregrine Falcons
Wayne State University.description: Peregrine falcons live on a balcony of Old Main's clock tower, and the university calls them its winged Warriors. Look up at the tower to spot them.

Wayne State University.name: Campus ArtWalk
Wayne State University.description: Around 30 donated outdoor sculptures make the campus an open-air gallery you can visit any time. Start at "City with Halo" in front of the Thompson Home and follow the ArtWalk map.

Wayne State University.name: Homecoming Game at Tom Adams Field
Wayne State University.description: Homecoming week ends with Warrior football at Tom Adams Field, and fans are asked to wear green and gold. Join the crowd and cheer on the Warriors.

Western Michigan University.name: The Bronco Statue
Western Michigan University.description: A 1,800-pound bronze bronco by sculptor Veryl Goodnight has stood on campus since 1997. It was first part of her larger work "The Day the Wall Came Down." Snap a photo with it.

Western Michigan University.name: Homecoming at Waldo Stadium
Western Michigan University.description: Each October WMU paints the town brown and gold for Homecoming, ending with Broncos football at Waldo Stadium. Join the crowd in the stands.

Western Michigan University.name: National Champions at Lawson Arena
Western Michigan University.description: The Broncos won their first men's ice hockey national championship in 2025. Catch a game at Lawson Arena and look for the championship banner.

Western Michigan University.name: Up Prospect Hill to Heritage Hall
Western Michigan University.description: WMU began on Prospect Hill, where East Hall opened in 1905 and a trolley once carried people up the slope. Walk up to Heritage Hall, the restored East Hall, and the North Hall portico beside it.

Grand Valley State University.name: Little Mac Bridge and the Ravines
Grand Valley State University.description: Students voted the ravines and the Little Mac Bridge the most beautiful spot on campus. Cross the footbridge and look down at the stream below.

Grand Valley State University.name: Carillon Music at Cook Tower
Grand Valley State University.description: Every week the university carillonist plays music, from Bach to pop songs, on the bells of the Cook Carillon Tower. If you hear bells, someone is up there playing live.

Grand Valley State University.name: Zumberge Pond
Grand Valley State University.description: Lakers love to study, eat or just relax on the steps beside Zumberge Pond in any season. Take a seat and enjoy the view.

Grand Valley State University.name: View from the Library Roof
Grand Valley State University.description: The roof of the Mary Idema Pew Library gives a sweeping view of the Allendale campus, a student favorite when the leaves change in fall. Go up and take in the view.

Grand Valley State University.name: Laker Football at Lubbers Stadium
Grand Valley State University.description: Lubbers Stadium officially seats 10,444 but often holds thousands more fans, with a record crowd of 17,007 in 2021. Join them for a Lakers home game.

Yale University.name: Rub Woolsey's Foot
Yale University.description: Generations of students have rubbed the protruding foot of the bronze statue of President Theodore Dwight Woolsey on Old Campus for good luck. Visitors can give the shiny foot a rub too.

Yale University.name: Hear the Harkness Carillon
Yale University.description: Students in the Yale Guild of Carillonneurs play the carillon in Harkness Tower twice a day during the school year, at 12:30 and 5:30 p.m., plus Friday concerts in summer. Visitors can listen from the streets and courtyards nearby.

Yale University.name: Visit the Women's Table
Yale University.description: Maya Lin's 1993 Women's Table in front of Sterling Memorial Library is carved with a spiral of numbers showing how many women studied at Yale each year since 1701. Visitors can walk up and read the spiral.

Harvard University.name: Touch John Harvard's Left Foot
Harvard University.description: Touching the left foot of the John Harvard statue in Harvard Yard is said to bring good luck, and it has been polished to a golden shine. Guides call it the 'statue of three lies', and visitors often pose for a photo with it.

Harvard University.name: Read Both Sides of Dexter Gate
Harvard University.description: Dexter Gate on Massachusetts Avenue reads 'Enter to grow in wisdom' on the outside and 'Depart to serve better thy country and thy kind' on the inside. Visitors can walk through and read both inscriptions.

Harvard University.name: Sheriffs at Johnston Gate
Harvard University.description: For centuries, the sheriffs of Middlesex and Suffolk Counties have ridden into Harvard Yard on horseback on Commencement Day, traditionally through Johnston Gate. Visitors can see the 1889 gate, the Yard's main entrance, at any time.

Massachusetts Institute of Technology.name: MIThenge
Massachusetts Institute of Technology.description: On a few days around mid-November and late January, the setting sun lines up with the Infinite Corridor and shines down its whole length. Crowds gather in the corridor to watch the light pour through.

Massachusetts Institute of Technology.name: Smoot markers on the Harvard Bridge
Massachusetts Institute of Technology.description: The Harvard Bridge sidewalk is painted with marks measuring its length in 'smoots', the height of 1958 pledge Oliver Smoot. Walk the bridge to find the 'Halfway to Hell' mark and the final '364.4 smoots plus or minus one ear'.

Princeton University.name: FitzRandolph Gate superstition
Princeton University.description: Campus legend says students who walk out through FitzRandolph Gate before graduation will not finish their degree, so undergraduates avoid it until Commencement. Visitors can see the gate on Nassau Street and decide for themselves which way to walk.

Princeton University.name: Arch sings at Blair Arch
Princeton University.description: Blair Arch, the largest arch on campus, is where many of Princeton's a cappella 'arch sings' take place. Stop under the arch to hear its echo, or catch a free evening concert.

Princeton University.name: Big Cannon on Cannon Green
Princeton University.description: A Revolutionary-era cannon has been buried muzzle-down on Cannon Green behind Nassau Hall since 1840, and it is slowly sinking. Visitors can see the exposed end; the green is also where the bonfire is lit when Princeton beats both Harvard and Yale in football.

Cornell University.name: Founders' statues and footprints
Cornell University.description: Legend says the statues of Ezra Cornell and Andrew Dickson White will walk off their pedestals and shake hands on the Arts Quad under certain impossible conditions, and painted footprints between them mark the legend. Look for the footprints and pose between the two founders.

Cornell University.name: Cornell Chimes in McGraw Tower
Cornell University.description: Student chimesmasters play the 21-bell Cornell Chimes in McGraw Tower in three concerts a day during the academic year, and visitors are welcome at all of them. Listen from Ho Plaza or the Arts Quad.

Cornell University.name: Dragon Day
Cornell University.description: On the Friday before spring break, first-year architecture students parade a huge handmade dragon past Sibley Hall toward the Arts Quad. Visitors can line the route and watch it go by.

Columbia University.name: Find the owl on Alma Mater
Columbia University.description: An owl, a symbol of wisdom, is hidden in the folds of Alma Mater's robe near her leg, and superstition says the first new student to find it becomes valedictorian. Visitors can hunt for the owl on the statue in front of Low Library.

Columbia University.name: Low Steps
Columbia University.description: The wide steps of Low Memorial Library, nicknamed 'Low Beach', are Columbia's favourite meeting spot. Sit on the steps and take in the view down to Butler Library.

Columbia University.name: The Sundial
Columbia University.description: The 1914 Class of 1885 Sundial at the centre of College Walk lost its granite ball in 1946, but its platform remains a classic gathering place and free-speech corner. It is also where the winter tree lighting and Yule Log ceremonies begin.

Columbia University.name: College Walk tree lighting
Columbia University.description: Each early December, the trees along College Walk are lit in a ceremony with a cappella music and hot chocolate, and the lights stay on until the end of February. Walk College Walk after dark in winter to see them.

University of Pennsylvania.name: The Button
University of Pennsylvania.description: Claes Oldenburg's Split Button sits on College Green, and student lore says it is the button that popped off Benjamin Franklin's vest, rolled down Locust Walk and split in two. It is a central campus landmark and a popular photo stop.

University of Pennsylvania.name: Ivy Day stones on College Hall
University of Pennsylvania.description: Since 1873 each graduating class has set an engraved Ivy Stone into a campus building, and there are now nearly 200 around campus. Start at College Hall and look for the class-year stones in the walls.

University of Pennsylvania.name: Hey Day on Locust Walk
University of Pennsylvania.description: Each spring, juniors in straw-style hats march down Locust Walk to College Hall to be declared seniors, a tradition dating back to Class Day in 1865. Visitors can watch the procession pass along the walk.

Brown University.name: Van Wickle Gates
Brown University.description: The centre Van Wickle Gates open only for Convocation and Commencement, and superstition says a student who passes through them more than twice will not graduate. Visitors can see the 1901 wrought-iron gates on Prospect Street and walk through the side gates instead.

Brown University.name: Bronze Bruno
Brown University.description: A seven-foot bronze of Bruno, Brown's bear mascot, stands on the College Green on a pedestal holding a slate rock said to be one Roger Williams stepped on in 1636. Stop by for a photo with the mascot.

Dartmouth College.name: Dartmouth Night Bonfire
Dartmouth College.description: Each Homecoming weekend a large bonfire is built on the Green and first-year students run laps around it, one for each year of their class number. Visitors can watch the parade and the lit bonfire from around the Green.

Dartmouth College.name: Winter Carnival Snow Sculpture
Dartmouth College.description: Every February for Winter Carnival, students build a large themed snow sculpture on the Green. Visitors can stop by to see and photograph it.

Dartmouth College.name: Warner Bentley's Nose
Dartmouth College.description: Students rub the nose of the statue of Warner Bentley in the Hopkins Center for the Arts for good luck, which has left it discoloured. Visitors to the Hop can find the statue and give it a rub.

Dartmouth College.name: The Bema and the Old Pine
Dartmouth College.description: On Class Day seniors gather at the Bema, a natural amphitheatre in College Park, then walk up the hill to the stump of the Old Pine for a farewell ceremony that dates to the 1830s. Visitors can walk through College Park to see both spots.

Georgetown University.name: Healy Hall Seal
Georgetown University.description: A mosaic Georgetown seal is set into the ground at the central entrance to Healy Hall, and students walk around it because legend says stepping on it means you won't graduate. Visitors can see the seal and watch students sidestep it.

Georgetown University.name: The Exorcist Steps
Georgetown University.description: The steep stone staircase from Prospect Street down to M Street appears in the final scene of The Exorcist, written by alumnus William Peter Blatty, and Hoyas make a point of running up them. Visitors can climb the public steps and take a photo.

Johns Hopkins University.name: The Gilman Hall Seal
Johns Hopkins University.description: Legend says a student who steps on the university seal in the Gilman Hall foyer won't graduate, so it's roped off. Have a look, then walk around it.

Johns Hopkins University.name: The Painted Blue Jay
Johns Hopkins University.description: Student groups repaint the Blue Jay statue to mark events and celebrations. Stop by to see what colors it's wearing today.

Johns Hopkins University.name: Lacrosse at Homewood Field
Johns Hopkins University.description: Lacrosse is the signature sport at Hopkins, and home games at Homewood Field draw big crowds. Catch a game and cheer on the Blue Jays.

Johns Hopkins University.name: The Beach
Johns Hopkins University.description: "The Beach" is the big lawn by the Eisenhower Library on Charles Street, where students study, picnic and play. Spread out a blanket and watch the sunset.

Johns Hopkins University.name: Spring Fair
Johns Hopkins University.description: Every spring since 1972, students have run Spring Fair, a weekend festival with vendors, food, rides and music that draws Baltimore residents too. Visit in April to join in.

Johns Hopkins University.name: The Art Museum Next Door
Johns Hopkins University.description: The Baltimore Museum of Art sits just steps from campus, and admission is free. Add it to your campus visit.

New York University.name: Washington Square Arch
New York University.description: The arch belongs to the city, but it has become the unofficial symbol of NYU, whose buildings ring the park. Take a photo with the arch and Fifth Avenue behind it.

New York University.name: Bust of Sylvette
New York University.description: In the plaza between the Silver Towers stands a huge enlargement of Picasso's Bust of Sylvette, made with Carl Nesjar. Walk into the courtyard to see it up close.

New York University.name: Gould Plaza
New York University.description: This plaza off West 4th Street, framed by the Stern School and the Courant Institute, is where NYU students gather after classes. Look for the purple NYU flags on the buildings around it.

New York University.name: Grey Art Museum
New York University.description: NYU's fine art museum, known as the Grey Art Gallery until 2023, now has larger galleries at 18 Cooper Square. Visit to see the university's collection, including modern Asian and Middle Eastern art.

Carnegie Mellon University.name: The Fence
Carnegie Mellon University.description: Painting the Fence in the middle of the Cut has been a tradition since the 1920s, and the original wooden fence once held the Guinness record as the most painted object. Walk by to see the newest coat of paint and message.

Carnegie Mellon University.name: Buggy Races
Carnegie Mellon University.description: During Spring Carnival, student teams push and free-roll sleek, unpowered buggies around a course in Schenley Park in a race officially called Sweepstakes. Head into the park to watch the heats.

Carnegie Mellon University.name: Spring Carnival Midway
Carnegie Mellon University.description: Each April, campus groups build multi-story booths with games for the Spring Carnival Midway on the College of Fine Arts parking lot. The carnival is open to the Pittsburgh community, so stop by and explore the booths.

Carnegie Mellon University.name: The Kiltie Band
Carnegie Mellon University.description: Formed in 1908, the Kiltie Band wears kilts in honor of Andrew Carnegie's Scottish roots and plays at every home football game. Catch a game to hear the band and see King Arthur's quest for the Grail between the third and fourth quarters.

University of Chicago.name: Reynolds Club Seal
University of Chicago.description: Legend says a student who steps on the University seal in the lobby of the Reynolds Club won't graduate in four years. Visitors can see the seal in the student union lobby and decide whether to test the myth.

University of Chicago.name: Cobb Gate Gargoyles
University of Chicago.description: By campus lore, the grotesques on Cobb Gate stand for the admissions officers and the climb of first- to fourth-year students, with the fourth-year at the top. Visitors can walk through the gate and look up to spot each figure.

University of Chicago.name: Botany Pond
University of Chicago.description: Botany Pond in Hull Court is a beloved campus spot where visitors come to see the ducklings and turtles. Stop by the pond for a quiet look at the wildlife and gardens.

University of Chicago.name: Rockefeller Chapel Carillon
University of Chicago.description: The 72-bell carillon at the top of Rockefeller Chapel is played in a daily recital, and student guild members give weekly concerts with bell-tower tours beforehand for anyone interested. Visitors can listen from the quad or join a tour.

University of Notre Dame.name: Main Building Front Steps
University of Notre Dame.description: Undergraduates avoid the front steps of the Main Building, as legend says using them means not graduating; seniors first walk them at graduation. Visitors are welcome to use the steps and take a photo under the Golden Dome.

University of Notre Dame.name: Light a Candle at the Grotto
University of Notre Dame.description: Students, alumni and visitors light candles and say a prayer at the Grotto of Our Lady of Lourdes; Notre Dame Magazine jokes you should leave double the suggested offering "just to be sure." Visitors can light a candle and read Tom Dooley's letter to Father Hesburgh there.

University of Notre Dame.name: Touchdown Jesus
University of Notre Dame.description: The Word of Life mural on the face of the Hesburgh Library, better known as Touchdown Jesus, is one of the campus landmarks where visiting families line up for photos. Visitors can pose in front of it by the reflecting pool.

University of Notre Dame.name: Fair Catch Corby
University of Notre Dame.description: The statue of Father William Corby with his arm raised, nicknamed Fair-Catch Corby, stands outside Corby Hall and is a classic campus photo stop. Visitors can pose beside it.

University of Notre Dame.name: Lyons Hall Arch
University of Notre Dame.description: Campus superstition holds that a couple who kiss under the archway of Lyons Hall may get engaged before graduation. Visitors can walk through the arch and see it for themselves.

University of Michigan.name: The Block M on the Diag
University of Michigan.description: Superstition says stepping on the bronze M in the Diag before your first exam means you'll fail it, so students walk around it. Visitors can find the M at the centre of the Diag and take a photo beside it.

University of Michigan.name: Engineering Arch
University of Michigan.description: Legend says a couple who kiss under the West Hall engineering arch at midnight will eventually marry. Visitors can walk through the arch at the southeast corner of the Diag.

University of Michigan.name: The Cube
University of Michigan.description: Endover, a 15-foot steel cube balanced on one corner in Regents' Plaza, is mounted so that it spins with a push. Visitors can give it a spin.

University of Michigan.name: The Rock
University of Michigan.description: A large boulder at Hill Street and Washtenaw Avenue has been painted over and over since the 1950s by students and the public. Visitors can stop to see its latest coat of paint.

Illinois Institute of Technology.name: Pumpkin Launch
Illinois Institute of Technology.description: Every October during family weekend, student teams build catapults and trebuchets and compete to fling pumpkins for distance and accuracy on Ed Glancy Field. The event draws spectators from across Chicago.

Illinois Institute of Technology.name: S. R. Crown Hall
Illinois Institute of Technology.description: Crown Hall, home of the College of Architecture, is widely considered Mies van der Rohe's finest work and seems to float above the lawn on travertine steps. Visitors can see this landmark of modern architecture up close.

Illinois Institute of Technology.name: The Tube over the Campus Center
Illinois Institute of Technology.description: Rem Koolhaas's McCormick Tribune Campus Center has a stainless-steel tube carrying CTA Green Line trains right over its roof. Visitors can watch trains pass through the tube overhead.

University of Virginia.name: Edgar Allan Poe's Room
University of Virginia.description: Poe's student room at 13 West Range is kept furnished as an 1826 student room. Visitors look in through a glass door and can press a button to hear a recording about Poe's time at UVA.

University of Virginia.name: Painted Beta Bridge
University of Virginia.description: Since the latter half of the 20th century, students have painted messages on the Rugby Road bridge, from club events to birthdays and memorials. Stop by to see what is painted on it this week.

University of Virginia.name: Lighting of the Lawn
University of Virginia.description: Each December, a cappella performances on the Lawn end with a light show on the Rotunda. The lights around the Academical Village then stay lit every night until early January.

University of Virginia.name: Trick-or-Treating on the Lawn
University of Virginia.description: On Halloween, students living in the Lawn rooms hand out candy to local children, a tradition since the 1980s. Families line up along the 54 Lawn rooms.

Rice University.name: Through the Sallyport
Rice University.description: By tradition, Rice students pass through the Sallyport arch in Lovett Hall as they leave at graduation and avoid it until then. Stand under the arch and look across the Academic Quad.

Rice University.name: Skyspace at Sunset
Rice University.description: James Turrell's Twilight Epiphany Skyspace puts on a free light show at sunrise and sunset, as changing colored light transforms the sky seen through its roof opening. Arrive early for a seat.

Rice University.name: The Moon Speech Stadium
Rice University.description: In 1962 President Kennedy spoke at Rice Stadium and challenged the nation to reach the Moon by the end of the decade. Visit the stadium where the famous speech was given.

Rice University.name: The Marching Owl Band
Rice University.description: The Marching Owl Band, or MOB, is a scatter band: instead of marching in formation, it performs comic skits at football games. Catch its halftime show.

Rice University.name: A Tree for Every Student
Rice University.description: More than 4,000 trees and shrubs make the whole campus an arboretum, which gave rise to the legend that Rice has a tree for every student. Stroll the shady quads.

Emory University.name: The Gravity Monument
Emory University.description: Hidden in the trees off Dowman Drive is a pink marble monument that Roger Babson gave Emory in 1963 to honor the sciences. Many say it looks more like a tombstone in the woods. See if you can find it.

Emory University.name: Lullwater Preserve and Tower
Emory University.description: Lullwater Preserve is a 154-acre stretch of woods and water that walkers and joggers enjoy. Follow the trail to the old granite tower Walter Candler built beside his dam to power his house.

Emory University.name: Words Under the Eaves
Emory University.description: Henry Hornbostel set the look of the Quad with pink Georgia marble and red tile roofs. Look up under the eaves of the older buildings to find carved words naming what was once taught inside.

Emory University.name: Source Route
Emory University.description: Behind the Carlos Museum, a set of stairs leads down into Baker Woodland. It is part of an environmental sculpture installed in the 1970s. Take the steps into the woods.

Emory University.name: Robinson Clock Tower Bells
Emory University.description: The clock tower on Cox Hall carries carillon bells dedicated in 2001 to honor trustee J. William Robinson and his wife. Listen for them as you cross the campus.

Tulane University.name: Ride the St. Charles Streetcar
Tulane University.description: The St. Charles line has run since 1835 and is the oldest continuously operating streetcar line in the world. Ride it to the Tulane University stop in front of Gibson Hall.

Tulane University.name: Tiffany Windows on Woodward Way
Tulane University.description: Two Louis Comfort Tiffany stained-glass triptychs, made in the 1890s for a chapel at Newcomb College's old Garden District campus, now line the Woodward Way breezeway at the Newcomb Art Museum. Stop and look for them.

Tulane University.name: Rogers Memorial Chapel
Tulane University.description: More of Tulane's Tiffany stained glass is in the Myra Clare Rogers Memorial Chapel on the Newcomb side of campus. Peek inside to see the windows.

Tulane University.name: Maya Gallery in Dinwiddie Hall
Tulane University.description: The Middle American Research Institute has studied the Maya since 1924. Its gallery on the third floor of Dinwiddie Hall is open to the public on weekdays.

Washington University in St. Louis.name: Don't Step on the Seal
Washington University in St. Louis.description: Campus legend says that stepping on the university seal under Brookings Hall will keep you from graduating, though touching the Chancellor's Medallion breaks the curse. Find the seal and walk around it.

Washington University in St. Louis.name: Declaration of Independence in Olin
Washington University in St. Louis.description: Olin Library displays a broadside copy of the Declaration of Independence, printed before the document was signed to spread the news across the colonies. Stop by the exhibit to see it in person.

Washington University in St. Louis.name: Lunch at Holmes Lounge
Washington University in St. Louis.description: The old library reading room in Ridgley Hall is now Holmes Lounge, one of the most beautiful rooms on campus. Grab lunch there and take in the surroundings.

Washington University in St. Louis.name: The Painted Underpass
Washington University in St. Louis.description: The underpass linking the South 40 to the main campus is covered in painted announcements for campus events. Walk through to see the latest designs.

Washington University in St. Louis.name: Assembly Series in Graham Chapel
Washington University in St. Louis.description: Graham Chapel hosts the Assembly Series, the university's long-running lecture program, which has brought speakers such as Eleanor Roosevelt and Gloria Steinem to campus. Check the schedule and catch a talk.

Stanford University.name: Class Plaques of the Inner Quad
Stanford University.description: Each graduating class buries a time capsule and marks it with a bronze plaque in the walkway around the Inner Quad, starting with 1896 in front of Memorial Church. Walk the arcade and look for a class year.

Stanford University.name: Hoover Tower Observation Deck
Stanford University.description: An observation deck 250 feet up gives wide views of campus, and on clear days the San Francisco skyline. The tower also holds a carillon given by the Belgian American Educational Foundation.

Stanford University.name: Memorial Church Cherubs
Stanford University.description: Local legend says the stone cherubs carved above the chancel niches and on the pillar capitals were modelled on children living on campus while the church was built. Look up and find them inside the church.

University of California, Berkeley.name: The Campanile
University of California, Berkeley.description: Ride the elevator to the observation deck of Sather Tower for views of campus and the Bay. The carillon plays short daily concerts, and on the last day of classes it plays "They're Hanging Danny Deever in the Morning" before going silent for finals.

University of California, Berkeley.name: The 4.0 Ball
University of California, Berkeley.description: Students rub or kiss the stone ball in front of the Campanile for good luck, especially after stepping on a University seal. Give it a touch on your way past.

University of California, Berkeley.name: Athena at Doe Library
University of California, Berkeley.description: Legend says walking under the statue of Athena at the Doe Library entrance gives you wisdom, but walking back out under her takes it away. Students leave by the back doors to keep it.

University of California, Berkeley.name: Hike to the Big C
University of California, Berkeley.description: A walk from near the Foothill parking area leads up to the Big C on the hillside above campus, a hike almost every Cal student makes. Enjoy the view back over campus and the Bay.

University of California, Los Angeles.name: Rub the Bruin Bear's Paw
University of California, Los Angeles.description: Students rub the paw of the Bruin Bear statue in Bruin Plaza for good luck during finals week. Visitors stop for a photo and a paw rub.

University of California, Los Angeles.name: Skip the Sixth Step
University of California, Los Angeles.description: Legend says anyone who steps on the sixth step of Janss Steps will have bad luck and graduate a quarter late. Many students hop over it on the way up.

University of California, Los Angeles.name: Inverted Fountain
