University of California, Los Angeles.description: New students are "Bruintized" at this 1968 fountain, whose water drops into a well instead of spraying up. Tradition says they then avoid touching the water until graduation, so visitors look but do not touch.

University of Washington.name: Cherry Blossoms in the Quad
University of Washington.description: Visiting the Yoshino cherry trees in the Quad when they bloom each spring is a must-do UW tradition. Expect crowds of students and visitors taking photos at peak bloom.

University of Washington.name: Rainier Vista
University of Washington.description: The view down Rainier Vista past Drumheller Fountain is protected so nothing can block Mount Rainier from Red Square. On a clear day, stand at the top for the best view on campus.

University of Washington.name: Sylvan Grove Columns
University of Washington.description: Four cedar columns from the UW's first downtown building stand in Sylvan Grove and represent loyalty, industry, faith and efficiency. New students touch one when they arrive and again at graduation; visitors can see them in the grove.

University of Washington.name: The Wave at Husky Stadium
University of Washington.description: UW says the famous stadium wave began at Husky Stadium during a 1981 football game. Join in when it rolls around the stands on game day.

McGill University.name: Chimes of the Roddick Gates
McGill University.description: The Roddick Gates, McGill's formal entrance on Sherbrooke Street, carry four clocks whose bells strike the Westminster Quarters. Walk through the gates onto campus and listen for the chimes.

McGill University.name: James McGill's Tomb
McGill University.description: The remains of founder James McGill rest in a monument in front of the Arts Building, moved there from a Montreal cemetery and consecrated in 1875. Visitors can stop by the founder's tomb on the lower campus.

McGill University.name: Photo at the Three Bares
McGill University.description: The Three Bares fountain, unveiled at Spring Convocation in 1931 in a tree-lined dell near the Redpath Museum, appears in countless convocation photographs. Visitors can take their own photo at this well-known campus landmark.

University of Toronto.name: Reznikoff's Gargoyles
University of Toronto.description: University College's best-known ghost story says stonemason Ivan Reznikoff was killed by a rival while the building was going up in the 1850s. Visitors can look for the two gargoyles said to show the rivals' faces near UC's southwest corner, where a door is said to bear an axe mark.

University of Toronto.name: The Weeping Stone Face
University of Toronto.description: Campus ghost lore includes a carved stone face at Hart House that is said to have wept water from one eye. Visitors to Hart House can look for the face among its Gothic stonework.

University of Toronto.name: Soldiers' Tower Carillon
University of Toronto.description: The 51 bells of the Soldiers' Tower carillon honour university members who died in the World Wars, and they ring out for free public recitals and around convocation. Listen from the Hart House Circle lawn or the University College quadrangle.

University of British Columbia.name: The Great Trek Cairn
University of British Columbia.description: This stone cairn on Main Mall marks the 1922 Great Trek, when students marched to Point Grey to push the government to finish the campus, and it was built from stones gathered on site. A ceremony is held there each September during Homecoming, and visitors can read its inscription any time.

University of British Columbia.name: The Painted Engineering Cairn
University of British Columbia.description: Engineering students look after a concrete monument on Main Mall that is repainted for causes, anniversaries and campus events. Visitors can stop by to see its latest paint job.

University of British Columbia.name: Ladner Clock Tower Chimes
University of British Columbia.description: The Ladner Clock Tower in front of the Main Library chimes on the hour, and its carillon plays short sets during the day and on special occasions such as convocation. Visitors can listen from the Library Garden.

National Autonomous University of Mexico.name: Day of the Dead Megaofrenda
National Autonomous University of Mexico.description: Each year around Day of the Dead, UNAM schools and offices build a giant collective offering of altars, long held at Las Islas, the central lawn of Ciudad Universitaria. Visitors can walk among the altars for free in early November.

National Autonomous University of Mexico.name: Central Library Mosaic
National Autonomous University of Mexico.description: Juan O'Gorman's stone mosaic covers all four sides of the Central Library, each side showing a different era of Mexican history. Walk around the building to see every side and take a photo of this campus icon.

National Autonomous University of Mexico.name: Rectory Tower Murals
National Autonomous University of Mexico.description: The Rectory Tower carries three murals by David Alfaro Siqueiros and, at the top, the university coat of arms with the motto 'Por mi raza hablará el espíritu'. Visitors can view the murals and the shield from the esplanade.

National Autonomous University of Mexico.name: Diego Rivera Relief at the Olympic Stadium
National Autonomous University of Mexico.description: The main entrance of the Estadio Olímpico Universitario features a relief by Diego Rivera made of naturally coloured stones, and the stadium still has its 1968 Olympic cauldron. Visitors can see the relief from outside the stadium.

California Institute of Technology.name: The Fleming Cannon
California Institute of Technology.description: A Franco-Prussian War-era cannon rests on its wheels in front of Fleming House and is fired only for big moments like commencement. MIT students once hauled it across the country as a prank. Stop by to see it.

California Institute of Technology.name: The Turtle Pond
California Institute of Technology.description: Dozens of turtles, mostly red-eared sliders, live in the pond in Throop Memorial Garden, where Caltech's first building once stood. Look for them sunning on the rocks, but don't feed them.

California Institute of Technology.name: Watson Lectures
California Institute of Technology.description: For about a century Caltech scientists have explained their work in free public talks, today called the Watson Lectures and held at Beckman Auditorium. Catch one in person or online.

California Institute of Technology.name: Halloween Pumpkin Drop
California Institute of Technology.description: Every Halloween, students drop pumpkins frozen in liquid nitrogen from the top of Caltech Hall, the former Millikan Library, while a crowd watches for a spark. The name nods to Millikan's famous oil-drop experiment.

California Institute of Technology.name: Tournament Park
California Institute of Technology.description: The athletic field at Tournament Park, on the south side of campus, hosted the first Rose Bowl games. Walk past the track to see where the famous game began.
